summary: Source decomposition of the quaternionic Gross-Zagier programme from Yuan-Zhang-Zhang's monograph (Chapter 1 and Sec. 7.1 read in full) together with the authors' published erratum (read in full). Covers: the three normalisation choices that govern every statement (root-number convention, dichotomy set, toric measure) in their ERRATUM-CORRECTED form; the Neron-Tate height with Thms. 7.1-7.2 and the Poincare pairing; flat and xi-admissible arithmetic divisors with the Faltings-Hriljac index theorem (Thm. 7.4) and its sign; the normalised Hodge class xi_U, deg L_U = vol(X_U) and the space pi_A = Hom^0_xi(X,A) of xi-normalised parametrisations with strict GL(2)-type derived from Eichler-Shimura; Saito-Tunnell multiplicity one with the corrected epsilon dichotomy and the local toric functional alpha_v; the Waldspurger formula with its exact constant and its two Siegel-Weil inputs; the generating series, the push-forward definition of the special cycles (erratum-corrected), the geometric kernel and the arithmetic theta lifting; the degenerate Schwartz functions with their four stated effects and the nearby-quaternion approximation argument; and the main Theorem 1.2 with its vacuous and essential cases, the projector reformulation Thm. 3.15, and the classical Thm. 1.1 as quoted. Chapters 2-6 and 8 and Secs. 3.1-3.6, 7.2-7.4 of the book are NOT read: every proof step recorded from them comes from the authors' own plan of the proof and is flagged as such. GZ.9 is not started. The original Gross-Zagier paper and Zhang's 'Admissible pairing on a curve' are present in the library but have NO usable text layer.

nodes.title: Root-number convention, dichotomy set and Haar-measure normalisation (with the published corrections)
nodes.statement: Three normalisation choices govern every statement of the quaternionic Gross-Zagier and Waldspurger formulae, and all three were misprinted in the first printing of Yuan-Zhang-Zhang and are fixed by the authors' erratum. (1) ROOT-NUMBER CONVENTION. epsilon(1/2, pi, chi) may be taken either as the root number of the base-change L-function over E twisted by chi, or as that of the Rankin-Selberg L-function over F; the two differ by eta(-1). Yuan-Zhang-Zhang take the FIRST convention, and with it the Saito-Tunnell dichotomy reads epsilon(1/2, pi, chi) = chi(-1) epsilon(B), NOT chi(-1) eta(-1) epsilon(B). (2) DICHOTOMY SET. Correspondingly Sigma(A,chi) = {places v of F : epsilon(1/2, pi_{A,v}, chi_v) is not chi_v(-1)}, without the factor eta_v(-1). (3) MEASURE. The local Haar measures dt_v on E_v^x/F_v^x are normalised so that the product measure gives vol(E^x \ E_A^x / A^x) = 2 L(1, eta) -- NOT the Tamagawa measure; the factor 4 L(1,eta)^2 in the main theorem 'comes from the measure', not from the Tamagawa measure. In addition the rationality statement for alpha_v(f1 tensor f2) holds 'for all non-archimedean places v', not for all places.
hypotheses: the two root-number conventions differ by exactly eta(-1); a statement that does not say which is in force is ambiguous at the level of a sign

the measure normalisation vol(E^x \ E_A^x / A^x) = 2 L(1,eta) is a NON-Tamagawa normalisation; the erratum also deletes the sentence asserting that the Tamagawa number of SO(V) is 2L(1,eta), 2, 2 in the three relevant cases

the Petersson pairing used to normalise the local pairings is taken with the Tamagawa measure, which has volume 2 on B^x \ B_A^x / A^x -- a different measure from the toric one; the two must not be conflated
the local functionals alpha_v are defined with the normalising factor L(1,eta_v) L(1,pi_v,ad) / (zeta_{F_v}(2) L(1/2, pi_v, chi_v)), so a change of any of these local factors changes alpha_v
proofSteps: Erratum item 5 states the corrected Saito-Tunnell dichotomy and explains the source of the discrepancy: 'In the literature, there are two conventional ways to define the root number epsilon(1/2,pi,chi) ... The ratio of these two definitions are eta(-1). This paper takes the first convention.'
Erratum item 2 propagates the same correction to the definition of Sigma(A,chi) on book p. 8.
Erratum items 4, 10, 13 and 15 replace the Tamagawa normalisation of the toric measure by the explicit normalisation vol = 2 L(1,eta) and delete the corresponding Tamagawa-number sentence.
Erratum item 3 restricts the rationality assertion for alpha_v to non-archimedean v.
acceptance: Check any downstream use of the dichotomy against the CORRECTED form epsilon(1/2,pi,chi) = chi(-1) epsilon(B); a source that includes eta(-1) is using the other root-number convention and its Sigma set differs.
Check that the constant 4 L(1,eta)^2 in Thm. 1.2 and 8 L(1,eta)^2 in Thm. 1.4 are traced to the toric measure normalisation vol = 2 L(1,eta) and not re-derived from a Tamagawa computation.

Check that alpha_v is claimed rational only at non-archimedean v.

nodes.title: The Neron-Tate height, its quadraticity and the Poincare pairing between A and A-dual
nodes.statement: Fix a number field F; the normalisation of heights depends on F. The standard height on P^n_F is h(x) = (1/[K:F]) sum over places w of K of log max{|x_0|_w, ..., |x_n|_w}, independent of the homogeneous coordinates and of the field K containing them. For a projective variety Y/F and a line bundle L there is a Weil height h_L : Y(Fbar) -> R, determined by L up to a bounded function, defined first for very ample L by an embedding and then for general L by writing L = L_1 tensor L_2^{-1}. For an abelian variety A/F and a SYMMETRIC line bundle L (i.e. [-1]^* L is isomorphic to L), the Neron-Tate height is h-hat_L(x) = lim_{N -> infinity} N^{-2} h_L(Nx); the limit exists and is independent of the choice of Weil height. Theorem 7.1: if L is ample and symmetric then (1) h-hat_L(x) >= 0 with equality exactly for torsion x, and (2) h-hat_L is quadratic: h-hat_L(x+y) + h-hat_L(x-y) = 2 h-hat_L(x) + 2 h-hat_L(y). Hence <x,y>_L = h-hat_L(x+y) - h-hat_L(x) - h-hat_L(y) is a pairing, positive definite modulo torsion, extending to a positive definite Hermitian pairing on A(Fbar)_C. Taking L = the Poincare bundle P on A x A-dual, which is symmetric, gives the bilinear Neron-Tate pairing <.,.>_NT : A(Fbar) x A-dual(Fbar) -> R, and Theorem 7.2 asserts <x,y>_L = <x, phi_L(y)>_NT for the polarisation phi_L(x) = T_x^* L tensor L^{-1}.
hypotheses: the normalisation of h depends on the chosen base number field F; a base change multiplies the arithmetic intersection identity by [L:F]
L must be SYMMETRIC for the limit defining h-hat_L to exist as stated, and AMPLE for the positivity and torsion characterisation of Thm. 7.1(1)
positive definiteness of <.,.>_L is only modulo torsion; the statement 'h-hat_L(x) = 0 iff x is torsion' is where Northcott-type finiteness enters
the Poincare bundle pairing is a pairing between A and its DUAL; identifying it with <.,.>_L requires the polarisation phi_L, per Thm. 7.2
proofSteps: The Weil height machine gives h_L up to bounded functions; the quadratic limit removes the ambiguity.
Theorem 7.1 is quoted by Yuan-Zhang-Zhang from Serre's book ('All the results here can be found in Serre's book [Se]'); the proofs are not reproduced there and were not read here.

Theorem 7.2 identifies the L-pairing with the Poincare pairing composed with the polarisation, which is what allows the Gross-Zagier statement to be written for the pair (A, A-dual) rather than for a single polarised A.

nodes.title: Flat and xi-admissible arithmetic divisors and the arithmetic Hodge index theorem
nodes.statement: Let X be a complete smooth (possibly disconnected) curve over a number field F, Div^0(X) the divisors of degree zero on EVERY connected component, and X a regular integral model over O_F with semistable reduction. An arithmetic divisor D-hat = (D, g_D) on X is FLAT if its intersection with every vertical divisor is zero; equivalently its curvature form omega_D vanishes and its intersection with every finite vertical divisor is zero. Flatness forces the generic fibre D_F to lie in Div^0(X). Theorem 7.4 (arithmetic Hodge index theorem of Faltings and Hriljac): for two flat arithmetic divisors D-hat_1, D-hat_2 on X, D-hat_1 . D-hat_2 = - <D_{1,F}, D_{2,F}>_NT. Since flat extensions exist only for degree-zero divisors, one fixes instead an arithmetic class xi-hat in Pic-hat(X) whose generic fibre has degree one on each connected component and calls D-hat xi-hat-ADMISSIBLE if, on each connected component: D-hat - deg(D) xi-hat is flat; the archimedean integral of g_D against c_1(xi-hat) vanishes at every archimedean place; and the intersection of the vertical part with xi-hat vanishes at every non-archimedean place. Every divisor D in Div(X) then has a UNIQUE xi-hat-admissible extension, depending on xi-hat. When the divisors are disjoint on the generic fibre the Neron-Tate height decomposes into a sum of local heights.
hypotheses: X must be regular with SEMISTABLE reduction for the statement as given; a non-semistable model requires base change first

Div^0 means degree zero on EVERY connected component, not merely total degree zero; X is allowed to be disconnected throughout (this is essential because the Shimura curves X_U are geometrically disconnected)
the Hodge index theorem is stated for FLAT arithmetic divisors; admissible extensions are introduced precisely because flat extensions exist only in degree zero
the sign in D-hat_1 . D-hat_2 = - <D_{1,F},D_{2,F}>_NT is part of the theorem and must be carried through every height computation
passing to a finite extension L/F modifies the identity by a factor [L:F] because of the height normalisation of GZ.1
the decomposition of the global height into local heights requires the divisors to be DISJOINT on the generic fibre; otherwise self-intersection terms appear
proofSteps: Yuan-Zhang-Zhang review the theory and attribute the arithmetic intersection theory to Arakelov and Gillet-Soule, the index theorem to Faltings and Hriljac, and admissible arithmetic extensions to Zhang; none of these proofs is reproduced in the section read.
The existence and uniqueness of the xi-hat-admissible extension is stated in Sec. 7.1.5 and used throughout Chapters 7 and 8.

In the application the degenerate Schwartz functions of Chapter 5 are chosen precisely so that there is no horizontal self-intersection and the intersections with the Hodge bundle vanish, which is what makes the local decomposition available.
acceptance: Check the disjointness hypothesis in every application; the source secures it by the Chapter 5 assumptions rather than by a general regularisation.
Check the sign convention of Thm. 7.4 against the height convention fixed at GZ.1.
Check that the admissible extension depends on the chosen xi-hat, so that a change of Hodge class changes the local heights even though the global height is unchanged.

Check that the intersection matrix of vertical fibre components is degenerate (it kills the whole fibre class), so that any 'inverse' used in a vertical correction is a generalised inverse on the orthogonal complement.

sources.excerpt: An arithmetic divisor D-hat on X is called flat if its intersection with any vertical divisor on X is zero. Equivalently, its curvature form omega_D is zero and its intersection with any finite vertical divisor on X is zero. It is easy to see that the flatness of D-hat = (D, g_D) forces the generic fiber D_F to lie in Div^0(X).
sources.match: Gives the definition of flatness in both equivalent forms and the consequence that the generic fibre has degree zero.

sources.excerpt: Theorem 7.4. Let D-hat_1 = (D_1, g_{D_1}) and D-hat_2 = (D_2, g_{D_2}) be two flat arithmetic divisors on X. Then D-hat_1 . D-hat_2 = - <D_{1,F}, D_{2,F}>_NT.
sources.match: Gives the arithmetic Hodge index theorem with its sign, as recorded in the statement.

sources.excerpt: The arithmetic divisor D-hat = (D, g_D) is called xi-hat-admissible if the following conditions hold on each connected component of X: The difference D-hat - deg D . xi-hat is flat; The integral over X_v(C) of g_D c_1(xi-hat) = 0 at any archimedean place v of F; The intersection (V . xi-hat)_v = 0 at any non-archimedean place v of F. Any divisor D in Div(X) has a unique xi-hat-admissible extension, which we denote by D-bar. It depends on xi-hat.
sources.match: Gives the three defining conditions of admissibility and the existence-and-uniqueness statement, including the dependence on xi-hat.

sources.excerpt: The Hodge index theorem gives a way to 'compute' the Neron-Tate height by flat arithmetic extensions. Flat arithmetic extensions are only for divisors of degree zero, so it is not enough in the computation. It is the reason to use admissible arithmetic extensions. If the divisors are disjoint on the generic fiber, we have a natural decomposition of the Neron-Tate height into local heights.
sources.match: States exactly why admissible extensions are needed and the disjointness hypothesis for the local decomposition.

nodes.title: The normalised Hodge class xi_U and the space pi_A of xi-normalised parametrisations
nodes.statement: The Shimura curve X_U carries a Hodge class L_U in Pic(X_U)_Q, the line bundle whose global sections are holomorphic modular forms of weight two; the system L = {L_U} is compatible under pullback along the projections pi_{U_1,U_2} : X_{U_1} -> X_{U_2}. If X_U is a modular curve -- which happens exactly when F = Q and Sigma = {infinity} -- then L_U is linearly equivalent to a linear combination of cusps; if F is not Q or Sigma is not {infinity} then X_U has no cusps and L_U is isomorphic to the canonical bundle for U small enough. For each geometric component alpha in pi_0(X_{U,Fbar}) set xi_{U,alpha} = L_{U,alpha}/deg(L_{U,alpha}) and xi_U = sum over alpha of xi_{U,alpha}, the NORMALISED Hodge class; deg L_{U,alpha} is independent of alpha because the geometric components are Galois conjugate, and Lemma 3.1 gives deg L_U = vol(X_U) with vol(X_U) the integral of dx dy/(2 pi y^2) over X_{U,tau}(C), a positive rational number; consequently deg(pi_{U_1,U_2}) = vol(X_{U_1})/vol(X_{U_2}). A simple abelian variety A/F is PARAMETRISED BY X if there is a non-constant morphism X_U -> A over F for some U; by Eichler-Shimura such an A is of strict GL(2)-type, i.e. M = End^0(A) is a FIELD and Lie(A) is free of rank one over M tensor_Q F. Define pi_A = Hom^0_xi(X,A) = direct limit over U of Hom^0_{xi_U}(X_U,A), where f in Hom_F(X_U,A) tensor_Z Q lies in pi_A exactly when sum_i a_i f(x_i) = 0 in A(Fbar)_Q for xi_U represented by the divisor sum_i a_i x_i. Equivalently pi_A = Hom^0(J,A) = direct limit of Hom^0(J_U,A).
hypotheses: A is SIMPLE and parametrised by X; strict GL(2)-type is a CONSEQUENCE (via Eichler-Shimura), not an assumption, and no claim is made that every abelian variety is parametrised by a Shimura curve
the normalisation of xi_U is by deg L_{U,alpha} on each GEOMETRIC component; the independence of alpha uses that the components are Galois conjugate
the cusp description of L_U is available exactly in the modular-curve case F = Q, Sigma = {infinity}; in all other cases X_U is proper and L_U is the canonical bundle only for U sufficiently small
the base-point condition defining Hom^0_{xi_U} is an identity in A(Fbar)_Q, so the morphisms are taken up to isogeny and denominators are allowed
proofSteps: Define L_U as the weight-two modular line bundle and normalise componentwise to get degree one on each geometric component.
Lemma 3.1 identifies deg L_U with the hyperbolic volume vol(X_U), which gives the degree formula for the projections and makes vol(X_U) the natural normalising factor throughout the book.
Eichler-Shimura theory gives the strict GL(2)-type statement for any A parametrised by X.
Factor any morphism X_U -> A through the Jacobian J_U to identify pi_A with Hom^0(J,A).
acceptance: Check the case distinction for L_U: a proof that uses the cusp description is valid only for F = Q and Sigma = {infinity}.
Check that xi_U has degree one on EACH geometric component, which is exactly the hypothesis required by the admissible-extension construction at GZ.2.
Check the identity deg L_U = vol(X_U) in one explicit modular-curve example, and that the volume is rational.
Check that strict GL(2)-type is derived and not assumed, and that Lie(A) free of rank one over M tensor_Q F is part of the definition.

sources.excerpt: Let A be a simple abelian variety defined over F. We say that A is parametrized by X if there is a non-constant morphism X_U -> A over F for some U. By the Eichler-Shimura theory, if A is parametrized by X, then A is of strict GL(2)-type in the sense that M = End^0(A) := End_F(A) tensor_Z Q is a field and Lie(A) is a free module of rank one over M tensor_Q F by the induced action.

nodes.title: Saito-Tunnell multiplicity one, the epsilon dichotomy, and the local toric functional alpha_v
nodes.statement: Let F be a local field, B a quaternion algebra over F with Hasse invariant epsilon(B) = 1 if B is M_2(F) and -1 if B is the division algebra, E either F + F or a quadratic field extension with a fixed embedding E -> B, eta the associated quadratic character of F^x, pi an irreducible admissible representation of B^x with central character omega_pi, and chi a character of E^x with omega_pi . chi|_{F^x} = 1. Put P(pi,chi) = Hom_{E^x}(pi tensor chi, C). THEOREM 1.3 (Tunnell, Saito): P(pi,chi) is at most one-dimensional, and is one-dimensional if and only if epsilon(1/2, pi, chi) = chi(-1) epsilon(B) -- in the root-number convention of GZ.0, i.e. viewing the L-function as the base change to E twisted by chi. Here epsilon(1/2,pi,chi) = epsilon(1/2,sigma,chi) = epsilon(1/2, sigma_E tensor chi) with sigma the Jacquet-Langlands transfer to GL_2(F). Since P(pi-tilde, chi^{-1}) has the same dimension, one works with P(pi,chi) tensor P(pi-tilde,chi^{-1}) and defines on it the canonical generator alpha_v(f1 tensor f2) = [L(1,eta_v) L(1,pi_v,ad) / (zeta_{F_v}(2) L(1/2,pi_v,chi_v))] times the integral over E_v^x/F_v^x of (pi_v(t) f1, f2)_v chi_v(t) dt. In the unramified situation -- E/F unramified, pi and chi unramified, vol(O_E^x/O_F^x) = 1, f1 and f2 spherical with (f1,f2) = 1 -- alpha_v(f1 tensor f2) = 1, so the product over all v is finite; and alpha is nonzero exactly when P(pi,chi) is nonzero.
hypotheses: omega_pi . chi|_{F^x} = 1 is required for P(pi,chi) to be nonzero for trivial reasons; it is a matching condition on central characters, not a normalisation

the CORRECTED dichotomy is epsilon(1/2,pi,chi) = chi(-1) epsilon(B); the first printing of the book had an extra eta(-1), which corresponds to the Rankin-Selberg rather than the base-change convention (see GZ.0)

the values alpha_v(f1 tensor f2) lie in L and are independent of the auxiliary complex embedding for all NON-ARCHIMEDEAN v (erratum item 3); the archimedean case is excluded from that rationality claim
alpha_v depends on the choice of the local invariant pairing (.,.)_v, normalised by the compatibility (.,.) = tensor_v (.,.)_v with the global duality pairing
the integral defining alpha_v is over E_v^x/F_v^x and is written 'formally'; the source defines it through an auxiliary embedding iota : L -> C
proofSteps: Theorem 1.3 is quoted from Tunnell and Saito; its proof is not in the book and was not read here.
The generator alpha = tensor_v alpha_v is well defined because alpha_v = 1 at almost all v by the unramified computation (Waldspurger, Sec. III-2, Lemme 10, cited by the source).
The rationality of alpha_v at non-archimedean v, and its independence of the embedding iota, are asserted in Sec. 1.3.2 as corrected by the erratum.
acceptance: Check that the one-dimensionality is used only as an upper bound where a statement must hold vacuously, and as an exact-dimension statement only under the dichotomy condition.
Check the unramified value alpha_v = 1 against the stated normalisation vol(O_E^x/O_F^x) = 1 and (f1,f2) = 1; a different local measure changes the value.
Check that a change of the local pairing (.,.)_v by a scalar c changes alpha_v by c^{-1}, and that the global compatibility (.,.) = tensor_v (.,.)_v pins the product.

nodes.title: The Waldspurger period formula and its proof through Shimizu lifting and Siegel-Weil
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field with adele ring A, B a quaternion algebra over F, E a quadratic field extension with a fixed embedding E -> B over F, pi an irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation of B_A^x with central character omega_pi, chi a character of E^x \ E_A^x with omega_pi . chi|_{A^x} = 1, and eta the quadratic character attached to E/F. Define P_chi(f) = integral over E^x \ E_A^x / A^x of f(t) chi(t) dt using the Haar measure of TOTAL VOLUME 1, and P_{chi^{-1}} on pi-tilde likewise. THEOREM 1.4 (Waldspurger): for f1 in pi and f2 in pi-tilde, P_chi(f1) . P_{chi^{-1}}(f2) = [zeta_F(2) L(1/2, pi, chi) / (8 L(1,eta)^2 L(1, pi, ad))] alpha(f1 tensor f2), where L(s,pi,chi) = L(s,sigma,chi) = L(s, sigma_E tensor chi) with sigma the Jacquet-Langlands lift, and alpha = tensor_v alpha_v with the local pairings normalised by (.,.)_Pet = tensor_v (.,.)_v, the Petersson pairing being taken with the TAMAGAWA measure of volume 2 on B^x \ B_A^x / A^x. The formula is an identity of two elements alpha and P_chi tensor P_{chi^{-1}} of P(pi,chi) tensor P(pi-tilde,chi^{-1}), which is nonzero only if Sigma(B) = Sigma(pi,chi) and is then one-dimensional with generator alpha.
hypotheses: chi is a character of E^x \ E_A^x with omega_pi . chi|_{A^x} = 1; Waldspurger's own statement assumed omega_pi trivial, and the source records that 'his proof goes through to the general case'
the period integral uses the PROBABILITY measure (total volume 1) on E^x \ E_A^x / A^x, whereas Waldspurger used the Tamagawa measure; the source flags this difference explicitly
the Petersson pairing uses the Tamagawa measure with volume 2 on B^x \ B_A^x / A^x; this is a different measure from the toric one of GZ.0
the identity is between two vectors in a space of dimension at most one; when Sigma(B) is not Sigma(pi,chi) the space is zero and the formula is vacuous

the constant is 8 L(1,eta)^2 in the Waldspurger formula, against 4 L(1,eta)^2 in the Gross-Zagier formula (Thm. 1.2); the factor-of-two difference is a genuine feature of the two normalisations and must not be transported
proofSteps: Start from the Shimizu (theta) lifting theta : S(B x A^x) tensor sigma -> pi tensor pi-tilde, where the Weil representation r of GL_2(A) x B_A^x x B_A^x acts on S(B_A x A^x) and the theta series is the double sum over u in F^x and x in B of r(g,(h_1,h_2)) Phi(x,u). (The book's p. 13 display omitted the inner sum over x in B; erratum item 6 restores it.)

Write f1 tensor f2 = theta(Phi tensor phi) and obtain P_chi(f1) P_{chi^{-1}}(f2) = (theta(., (chi,chi^{-1}), Phi), phi)_Pet, where theta(g,(chi,chi^{-1}),Phi) is the double toric integral of the theta kernel.

Use the integral representation (I(s,.,chi,Phi), phi)_Pet = (nonzero explicit constant) L((s+1)/2, sigma, chi), where I(s,g,chi,Phi) is the toric integral of the mixed theta-Eisenstein series I(s,g,Phi) = sum over u in F^x, x_1 in E, gamma in P^1(F) \ P^1(A) of delta(gamma g)^s r(gamma g) Phi(x_1,u).

The formula follows from the two identities (1.5.1) I(0,g,chi,Phi) = 2 theta(g,(chi,chi^{-1}),Phi) and (1.5.2) (I(0,.,chi,Phi),phi)_Pet = (constant) L(1/2,sigma,chi) alpha(f1 tensor f2). The source states that both are implied by the SIEGEL-WEIL formula with minor extra work: the first by Siegel-Weil on the quadratic space (E,q), the second by Siegel-Weil on (B_0,q) with B_0 the trace-zero elements of B.

nodes.title: The generating series, the geometric kernel, and the kernel identity
nodes.statement: For Phi in S(B_A x A^x) bi-invariant under an open compact U of B_f^x, the generating function on X_U is Z(g,Phi)_U = Z_0(phi)_U + w_U sum over a in F^x, x in U \ B_f^x / U of r(g) phi(x, a q(x)^{-1}) Z(x)_U, where phi is the archimedean average of Phi, w_U and Z_0(phi)_U are the constant terms, and Z(x)_U is the special cycle attached to the double coset U x U. The special cycle Z(x)_U must be defined as the PUSH-FORWARD (with multiplicities) of X_{U_x} under (pi_{U_x,U}, pi_{U_x,U} o T_x) : X_{U_x} -> X_U x X_U, NOT as the set-theoretic image; the first printing of the book defined it as the image and the erratum corrects this. Z(g,Phi)_U is an automorphic form in g in GL_2(A) with coefficients in Pic(X_U x X_U)_C; for X_U = X_0(N) and suitable Phi it recovers the classical series sum_{n >= 0} T_n e^{2 pi i n z}. Rescaling gives a compatible system Z-tilde(g,Phi) in Pic(X x X)_C, and the height series is Z-tilde(g,(h_1,h_2),Phi) = <Z-tilde(g,Phi)[h_1]^o, [h_2]^o>_NT with [h]^o = [h] - xi_{q(h)} the xi-normalised degree-zero class of the CM point T_h(P). The geometric kernel is the REGULARISED toric integral Z-tilde(g,chi,Phi) = integral^* over T(F) \ T(A) / Z(A) of Z-tilde(g,(t,1),Phi) chi(t) dt. The kernel identity (Theorem 3.21) is (I'(0,.,chi,Phi), phi)_Pet = 2 (Z-tilde(.,chi,Phi), phi)_Pet for all phi in sigma; the exact pointwise equality I'(0,g,chi,Phi) = 2 Z-tilde(g,chi,Phi) is NOT asserted. The bridge is the arithmetic theta lifting Z-tilde(Phi tensor phi) = (Z-tilde(g,Phi), phi)_Pet, for which (1.5.5) states Z-tilde(Phi tensor phi) = [L(1,pi,ad)/(2 zeta_F(2))] T(theta(Phi tensor phi)).
hypotheses: Phi must be bi-invariant under an open compact U, and phi denotes its archimedean average; the erratum (item 8) corrects the displayed generating function to use phi rather than Phi in the Schwartz factor
the special cycle is the proper push-forward with multiplicities; using the set-theoretic image changes the cycle whenever the map is not injective
the toric integral defining the geometric kernel is REGULARISED; it is not an absolutely convergent integral
the kernel identity is asserted only after pairing with cusp forms phi in sigma, i.e. after cuspidal projection; the source explicitly discusses 'the impossibility of the exact equality'
the CM classes are xi-normalised to degree zero via [h]^o = [h] - xi_{q(h)}, which is what makes the Neron-Tate pairing defined
proofSteps: Modularity of Z(g,Phi)_U in g, with coefficients in Pic(X_U x X_U)_C, is attributed by the source to 'the work of many people' and is proved in Chapter 4 Sec. 4.2 (not read here).

The identity (1.5.5) is proved in two steps in Chapter 4: first that both sides agree up to a constant, because each induces an element of the one-dimensional space Hom_{GL_2(A) x B_A^x x B_A^x}(S(V x A^x) tensor sigma, pi tensor pi-tilde) after decomposing H^{1,0}(X_tau) = direct sum over pi_1 of pi_1; second that the constant is as stated, by computing traces on H^{0,1}(X_{U,tau}).

The trace computation uses the Lefschetz fixed point theorem to reduce the trace of Z-tilde(Phi tensor phi) to the intersection number Delta_U . Z-tilde(Phi tensor phi), and hence to the pullback Delta_U^* Z(g,Phi)_U, which is an explicit generating function whose coefficients are CM points, Hodge classes or cusps. The source records that 'the computation is very complicated if X_U contains cusps' and compares with Hirzebruch-Zagier on Hilbert modular surfaces.
Given (1.5.5), the equivalence between the projector formulation (1.5.3) and the kernel identity (1.5.4) is immediate.
acceptance: Check the push-forward definition of Z(x)_U against the erratum; a set-theoretic image drops multiplicities and changes the generating series.
Check that the kernel identity is stated after pairing with phi in sigma, and that no pointwise identity of the two kernels is claimed.

Check the constant L(1,pi,ad)/(2 zeta_F(2)) in (1.5.5) against the constants in Thms. 1.2 and 1.4; it is the bridge that converts the Waldspurger-type constant 8 L(1,eta)^2 into the Gross-Zagier constant 4 L(1,eta)^2.

Check that the regularisation of the toric integral is defined before it is used, and that the degenerate Schwartz functions of GZ.7 are what remove the self-intersection and Hodge-class contributions.

nodes.title: Degenerate Schwartz functions, the local decomposition of both kernels, and the nearby-quaternion approximation
nodes.statement: For a non-archimedean place v define S^1(B_v x F_v^x) = {Phi_v : Phi_v(x,u) = 0 whenever v(u q(x)) >= -v(d_v) or v(u q(x_2)) >= -v(d_v)} with d_v the local different and x = x_1 + x_2 the decomposition along B_v = E_v + E_v j_v, and S^2(B_v x F_v^x) = {Phi_v : r(g) Phi_v(0,u) = 0 for all g in GL_2(F_v), u in F_v^x}. Assume Phi_v lies in S^1 at all ramified non-archimedean v nonsplit in E and at at least two non-archimedean v split in E. These assumptions (i) kill the self-intersections of CM points in the height series, (ii) kill the logarithmic singularities coming from both the derivatives and the local heights at v, (iii) kill the constant term of the generating series, and (iv) kill the arithmetic intersections with the Hodge classes. With them, both kernels decompose over the nonsplit places: Pr I'(0,g,chi,Phi) = sum over v nonsplit of I'(0,g,chi,Phi)(v), obtained from the Fourier expansion into local Whittaker functions with the derivative taken at v, and Z-tilde(g,chi,Phi) = sum over v nonsplit of Z-tilde(g,chi,Phi)(v), from the decomposition of a global arithmetic intersection into local ones. For archimedean v and GOOD non-archimedean v one proves I'(0,g,chi,Phi)(v) = 2 Z(g,chi,Phi)(v) by explicit computation. For the remaining BAD primes the local components are impossible to compute; instead one shows that each such I'(0,g,chi,Phi)(v) is APPROXIMATED by a coherent kernel I(0,g,chi,Phi(v)) built from the NEARBY quaternion algebra B(v) obtained by switching the Hasse invariant of B at v, and similarly for Z-tilde(g,chi,Phi)(v). Here Psi is approximated by Psi_0 if they agree on 1^S GL_2(A^S) for some finite S; if both are automorphic they are then equal, since GL_2(F) GL_2(A^S) is dense in GL_2(A).
hypotheses: the S^1 condition is imposed at ALL ramified non-archimedean places nonsplit in E and at AT LEAST TWO non-archimedean places split in E; both parts of the assumption are needed for the four listed effects

the reduction from the general kernel identity to the degenerate case is not formal: it uses the one-dimensionality of P(pi,chi) tensor P(pi-tilde,chi^{-1}) (Thm. 1.3), which reduces the identity to a single pair (Phi,phi) with alpha(theta(Phi tensor phi)) nonzero; the existence of such a Phi satisfying the degeneracy assumptions is a LOCAL problem solved in Chapter 5

the local decomposition of the geometric kernel requires no self-intersection, which is exactly what the degeneracy assumptions provide; without them the decomposition into local heights is not available (cf. GZ.2)
the approximation argument is valid because GL_2(F) GL_2(A^S) is dense in GL_2(A) and both sides are automorphic; it does not give a local identity at the bad places
proofSteps: Chapter 5 introduces the two classes of degenerate Schwartz functions and proves that the full kernel identity can be recovered from them, using Thm. 1.3.

Chapter 6 expands I(s,g,chi,Phi) as a Fourier series in local Whittaker functions, takes the derivative place by place, applies the cuspidal holomorphic projection Pr (which only changes the archimedean terms), and proves the approximation statement at bad v.
Chapter 7 decomposes the geometric kernel into local heights using the Arakelov theory of GZ.2, and proves the vanishing of the Hodge-class contributions under the Chapter 5 assumptions.
Chapter 8 computes the local heights of CM points in the archimedean, supersingular, superspecial and ordinary cases and proves the corresponding approximation statements at bad v.
The difference Pr I'(0,g,chi,Phi) - 2 Z-tilde(g,chi,Phi) is then approximated by a finite sum of coherent kernels I(0,g,chi,Phi(v)); automorphy plus density forces it to vanish.
acceptance: Check that the four listed effects of the degeneracy assumptions are each used where claimed; in particular that the vanishing of the Hodge-class contribution (Chapter 7 Sec. 7.3) is a theorem under those assumptions, not a general fact.
Check the reduction back to the general case: it needs BOTH Thm. 1.3's one-dimensionality and the local existence result of Chapter 5.
Check that Chapter 8's four local cases (archimedean, supersingular, superspecial, ordinary) are separate computations with separate hypotheses, and that the j-part (Sec. 8.5) is treated separately.
Check the density statement: GL_2(F) GL_2(A^S) dense in GL_2(A) is what converts approximation into equality, and it applies only to automorphic functions.

Here d_v is the local different of F at v, and x = x_1 + x_2 according to the orthogonal decomposition B_v = E_v + E_v j_v. Here are some major effects of the assumptions: Kill the self-intersections of CM points in the height series Z(g, (t1, t2), Phi). Kill the logarithmic singularities coming from both the derivatives and the local heights at v. Kill the constant term of the generating series Z(g, Phi)_U. This was the essential difficulty to remove the assumptions of mild ramifications in the work of Gross-Zagier and S. Zhang.

Here is a simple fact. If furthermore Psi is automorphic, then Psi = Psi_0 identically. It is true since GL2(F)GL2(A^S) is dense in GL2(A). ... I'(0, g, chi, Phi)(v) can be approximated by a coherent kernel function of the form I(0, g, chi, Phi(v)), where Phi(v) = Phi^v tensor Phi_v' in S(B(v)_A x A^x) is a Schwartz function based on the nearby quaternion algebra B(v) over F obtained by changing the Hasse invariant of B at v.

nodes.title: The general Gross-Zagier identity on quaternionic Shimura curves (YZZ Theorem 1.2)
nodes.statement: Let F be a totally real field, B a quaternion algebra over F with ramification set Sigma, X the associated Shimura curve system, A a simple abelian variety over F parametrised by X with M = End^0(A), pi_A = Hom^0_xi(X,A), E a quadratic field extension of F embedded in B, and chi a character of E^x \ E_A^x of finite order with omega_A . chi|_{A_F^x} = 1. THEOREM 1.2: for any f1 in pi_A and f2 in pi_{A-dual}, <P_chi(f1), P_{chi^{-1}}(f2)>_L = [zeta_F(2) L'(1/2, pi_A, chi) / (4 L(1,eta)^2 L(1, pi_A, ad))] alpha(f1,f2), as an identity in L tensor_Q C, where <.,.>_L : A(chi) x A-dual(chi^{-1}) -> L tensor_Q R is the L-linear Neron-Tate pairing induced by the M-linear pairing of GZ.1. The theorem compares the two elements alpha and <P_chi(.), P_{chi^{-1}}(.)>_L of the at-most-one-dimensional space P(pi_A,chi) tensor_L P(pi_{A-dual},chi^{-1}). If Sigma(B) is not Sigma(A,chi) the space is ZERO and both sides vanish, so the theorem is VACUOUS there; in the essential case Sigma(B) = Sigma(A,chi) the space is one-dimensional with generator alpha, epsilon(1/2,pi_A,chi) = -1, and the theorem is an explicit evaluation of the resulting scalar. An equivalent formulation (Theorem 3.15) states <T(f1 tensor f2) P_chi, P_{chi^{-1}}>_NT = [zeta_F(2) L'(1/2,pi,chi)/(4 L(1,eta)^2 L(1,pi,ad))] alpha(f1 tensor f2) in terms of the projector T(f1 tensor f2) in Hom^0(J,J-dual)_C; the equivalence uses T_alg(f1,f2) = f2-dual o f1 and the projection formula for height pairings. The classical case is Theorem 1.1 (Gross-Zagier): for f a newform of weight 2 on Gamma_0(N), K imaginary quadratic of odd fundamental discriminant D satisfying the Heegner condition that every prime factor of N splits in K, and chi a character of Pic(O_K), <P_chi(f), P_chi(f)>^H_NT = [h u^2 |D|^{1/2} / (8 pi^2 (f,f))] L'(f,chi,1).
hypotheses: A is SIMPLE and parametrised by X; chi has FINITE order; the central-character matching omega_A . chi|_{A_F^x} = 1 is required
the statement is an identity of two vectors in a space of dimension at most one, so it must be stated first as an identity of invariant bilinear forms; a zero pairing is never placed in a denominator
in the vacuous case Sigma(B) not equal to Sigma(A,chi) the identity holds trivially because both sides are zero
the dichotomy set Sigma(A,chi) is the ERRATUM-corrected one (see GZ.0): {v : epsilon(1/2,pi_{A,v},chi_v) not equal to chi_v(-1)}
the constant 4 L(1,eta)^2 comes from the toric measure normalisation vol(E^x \ E_A^x / A^x) = 2 L(1,eta), not from a Tamagawa measure

in the classical Theorem 1.1, h is the class number of K, u is HALF the number of units of O_K, (f,f) is the Petersson inner product, D is an ODD fundamental discriminant, and the Heegner condition is that every prime factor of N splits in K; under these hypotheses the sign of the functional equation is -1 and L(f,chi,1) = 0

sources.excerpt: Theorem 1.2. Assume omega_A . chi|_{A_F^x} = 1. For any f1 in pi_A and f2 in pi_{A-dual}, <P_chi(f1), P_{chi^{-1}}(f2)>_L = [zeta_F(2) L'(1/2, pi_A, chi) / (4 L(1, eta)^2 L(1, pi_A, ad))] alpha(f1, f2) as an identity in L tensor_Q C. Here <.,.>_L : A(chi) x A-dual(chi^{-1}) -> L tensor_Q R is the L-linear Neron-Tate height pairing induced by the M-linear Neron-Tate height pairing <.,.>_M between A(F) and A-dual(F).

sources.excerpt: If Sigma(B) not= Sigma(A, chi), the linear space is zero and thus both sides of the formula are zero. The theorem is vacuous in this case. In the essential case Sigma(B) = Sigma(A, chi), the linear space is one-dimensional and alpha is a generator. It follows that <P_chi(.), P_{chi^{-1}}(.)>_L must be a constant multiple of alpha. ... Note that epsilon(1/2, pi_A, chi) = -1 in this case.

sources.excerpt: Assume that K has an odd fundamental discriminant D, and satisfies the following Heegner condition: every prime factor of N is split in K. Then the sign of the functional equation of the L-series L(f, chi, s) is -1 and hence L(f, chi, 1) = 0. ... The construction of Heegner points P_chi(f) involves the idempotent in the Hecke algebra for Gamma_0(N), thus involves some denominators.

links.reason: The reduction of the general kernel identity to the degenerate Schwartz functions is NOT formal: the source says 'The key to recover (1.5.4) in the full case from these assumptions is Theorem 1.3'. One-dimensionality reduces the identity to a single pair (Phi,phi) with alpha(theta(Phi tensor phi)) nonzero, and the existence of such a Phi satisfying the degeneracy assumptions is a local problem.

The coherent Waldspurger identity is the template for the incoherent one: the geometric kernel Z-tilde(g,chi,Phi) 'takes the place of the kernel function theta(g,(chi,chi^{-1}),Phi) in the incoherent case', the analytic kernel I(s,g,chi,Phi) is defined by exactly the same formula, and the arithmetic theta lifting identity (1.5.5) is the incoherent counterpart of the (trivial) coherent statement.

GZ.7 computes the difference Pr I'(0,g,chi,Phi) - 2 Z-tilde(g,chi,Phi) of exactly the two kernels constructed at GZ.6; the degeneracy assumptions are imposed on the Schwartz function entering the generating series, and their four listed effects are all effects on that series and on the resulting height series.

The kernel identity, once proved in the degenerate case and extended by Thm. 1.3, is equivalent to Theorem 3.15 via the arithmetic theta lifting (1.5.5), and Theorem 3.15 is equivalent to Theorem 1.2 via the projector interpretation. GZ.7 is therefore the last proof step of GZ.8, not an independent statement.
